rule: ดี is two words: the quality (1-9) and the gall bladder (10-11), plus the Latin letter (12). The quality sense is so broad that its subdivisions rarely bite, so sense 1 keeps everything that just means good — including the compounds about thinking oneself good (อวดดี, ถือดี) and being tested on it (ลองดี). The subdivisions take only what their glosses name outright: sense 7, เก่ง, takes หัวดี, clever; sense 8, ชอบ, takes ดีใจ and ยินดี, which are gladness rather than goodness; sense 9, being in a normal state, takes ญาติดี, back on good terms, beside คืนดี already there. The gall bladder earns two: ดีซ่าน, jaundice, whose etymology is given as ดี + ซ่าน, and ดีเดือด, a rage that is literally the gall boiling. Sense 3 (สวย, งาม) stays empty — nothing in this list means beautiful.

notes.text:
**ดี** — ฤๅดี is a false-split the dictionary hands over: แผลงมาจาก ฤดี, แผลงมาจาก
รติ, จากสันสกฤต रति. It is Sanskrit *rati*, delight, not ดี. ดีฉัน likewise is the
pronoun (a variant of ดิฉัน < อีฉัน) and its ดี is the pronoun's own first
syllable. Sense 3 (สวย, งาม) stays empty: nothing in this list means beautiful.
